sections.title: Upgrade without starting over
sections.text: Ageing controls become a spares and support risk long before the plant does. We migrate obsolete DCS/PLC systems to current platforms with minimal downtime — keeping what still works and replacing what doesn't.

sections.title: The platform is a partnership. The expertise is ours.
rows: Titas LOC-C, J and Srikail, with SIL 3 safety system
Titas LOC-E and G, central DCS
Pidilite chemical plant DCS engineering, graphics, point configuration

sections.title: The 15-year questions
items: Redundancy: which parts are redundant — controller, power, network, I/O?
Cybersecurity: which IEC 62443 security level does the design target?
Obsolescence: what is the vendor's declared support horizon and migration path?

items.title: Assess
items.text: Audit the existing system, I/O and documentation.

items.title: Plan
items.text: Migration strategy, cutover sequence and rollback.

items.title: Stage
items.text: Configure and test the new system off-line (FAT).

items.title: Cut over
items.text: Phased changeover during a planned window, then SAT.

sections.title: The clock starts at obsolescence
sections.text: Once a platform goes end-of-life, every breakdown is a scramble for parts. Migrating on your schedule beats migrating on a failure's.

sections.title: Let's discuss your next project
sections.text: Tell us what you are planning. An engineer will reply, not a sales queue.
